items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1295

SPONSOR: GOUNARDES
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to requiring public employers
to adopt a plan for operations in the event of a declared state disaster
emergency involving a communicable disease; to amend the education law,
in relation to certain protocols for responding to a declared state
disaster emergency involving a communicable disease; and to amend a
chapter of the laws of 2020, amending the labor law relating to requir-
ing public employers to adopt a plan for operations in the event of a
declared public health emergency involving a communicable disease; and
amending the education law relating to certain protocols for responding
to a declared public health emergency involving a communicable disease;
and amending the education law relating to certain protocols for
responding to a declared public health emergency involving a communica-
ble disease, as proposed in legislative bills numbers S.8617B and
A.10832, in relation to requiring public employers to adopt a plan for
operations in the event of a declared state disaster emergency involving
a communicable disease

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this bill is to amend Chapter 168 of the Laws of 2020 to
remove contractors from the scope of such legislation and to clarify the
timeline for public employers to publish and finalize their plans for
operations in the event of a declared state disaster emergency involving
a communicable disease.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill would amend § 27-c of the Labor Law to remove
contractors from being included in public employers' plans for the
continuation of operations in the event that the Governor of New York
State declares a state disaster emergency involving a communicable
disease. It would also require such plans to include any other require-
ments determined by the New York State Department of Health, such as
contract tracing, testing, social distancing, hand hygiene, or mask
wearing.

Section two of the bill would eliminate the requirement for the New York
State Department of Labor to establish a dedicated hotline, in addition
to a webpage, for public employees to report alleged or believed
violations of state law.

Section three of the bill would amend § 2801-a of the Education Law to
make technical changes.

Section four of the bill would amend the effective date of the original
legislation to clarify that draft operation plans shall be published and
made available for comment to the applicable duly recognized or certi-
fied representatives of the employees and the relevant labor-management
committees no later than 150 days from such effective date and that such
plans shall be finalized by April 1, 2021.

Section five of the bill would establish the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):
N/A

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the private sector has received substantial guidance from the
State concerning which jobs are considered "essential" during the ongo-
ing COVID-19 pandemic, New York's public sector has not. In addition,
many civil servants across the state have continued to experience health
and safety challenges on the job with concern to personal protective
equipment, transportation, emergency housing, contact tracing and test-
ing, and protocols for cleaning and disinfecting work areas. These
employees, including state and local attorneys, teachers, social work-
ers, healthcare workers, EMS medics, corrections officers, firefighters,
and more, will be remembered for their service at the peak of the
pandemic and their contributions to the State's recovery, and thus
deserve to know that their health and safety is being protected. For
these reasons, this legislation would further ensure that public employ-
ers are better prepared for situations arising out of state disaster
emergencies involving communicable diseases in order to better safeguard
the health and wellbeing of New York's public workforce.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires public employers to adopt a plan for operations in the event of a declared state disaster emergency involving a communicable disease; establishes certain protocols necessary for responding to a declared state disaster emergency involving a communicable disease in an educational setting.
